reviewScope: Independent design-contract review only. This verdict does not mark DR-103 SATISFIED, does not qualify or demonstrate anything, and does not authorize implementation or docs/v2/implementation/.
summary: The RJ-1 provenance qualifier and triple entry key are repaired, but the lock contract still permits multi-component output and still bypasses unresolved compatibility semantics. Successor accounting also retains two SHOULD-FIX defects.

blockers.title: The purported single-component-only lock rule still permits a multi-component exact-pin lock
blockers.detail: lockSchema.resolutionInputs still accepts exact-pin pairs in the plural, and its amended semantics makes a request producible whenever every admitted manifest in the intended resolved set declares dependencies: []. It does not constrain request cardinality or resolved cardinality to one. A request containing two exact-pinned, dependency-free admitted components satisfies that rule: every manifest has an empty dependency array, no versionConstraint edge is closed, and the resulting lock has two resolved tuples. That directly contradicts ID-DEP-4's statement that the sole presently producible lock is an exact-pin of a single admitted component and TC-ACCEPT's statement that every multi-component lock is deferred to DR-111. The prompt's explicit attack therefore succeeds: a multi-component lock remains producible under the normative request semantics.
blockers.requiredRepair: For the presently producible form, require request length exactly one and resolved length exactly one, with the selected manifest's dependencies exactly empty; or explicitly allow independent multi-root locks and stop claiming that all multi-component locks are deferred.

blockers.title: The single-component exact pin still ignores the DR-111-owned compatibility meaning
blockers.detail: Every manifest is required to declare compatibility data whose surface vocabulary and window semantics belong to DR-111. resolutionInputs calls itself the complete declared input set and includes hostCoreVersion and platform, while lockSchema describes an exact-resolution record deterministically selected from those inputs. Admission may validate compatibility only structurally. v4 now says that copying an admitted exact pin does not evaluate compatibility windows and nevertheless calls the lock producible. That is the unresolved branch identified in the Codex v3 B1: either lock production evaluates the DR-111-owned compatibility relation, which is forbidden while DR-111 is OPEN, or it ignores a required declared input and cannot establish that the selected release is a valid resolution for the recorded host/platform. Narrowing dependencies to [] repairs the edge-constraint half only; it does not repair compatibility.
blockers.requiredRepair: Either defer every compatibility-bearing lock until DR-111, or define a separate non-validating custody/pin record that does not claim to be a completed compatible resolution. An assertion that compatibility is not evaluated does not discharge the required compatibility datum.

shouldFix.title: The successor claims to repair all Codex findings but leaves Codex S2 only half-addressed
shouldFix.detail: appliesFindingsOf records Codex S2 and says this successor repairs the dual REJECT findings, but the v4 repairLog has no Codex-S2 entry and sources remains byte-identical to v3. Appending the v4 review-guidance item repairs the guidance half; it does not repair the predecessor-scoped custody half: corpusHeadAtAuthoring and reMeasurementAtV2 still explicitly describe v2, while bindingSources say measuredAtAuthoring and SRC-PROTO says 'this authoring'. Three live whole-document source pins remain moved. Either record Codex S2 as partially repaired/carried, or scope the measurement fields explicitly to v2 and add v4 authoring custody.

The first 19 repairLog entries are value-identical to v3; eight entries are appended.

All nine substantive changes are addressed by the new repair entries at resolving pointers: collisionUniverse and RJ-2 (V3-B1); collisionUniverse, entry key, and shadowedBy (V3-B2); lock semantics and TC-ACCEPT (V3-B3); ID-DEP-4 consequence (V3-B4); manifest name type and semantics (Codex-S1). The live index key is consistently (stableId, version, scope) at collisionUniverse and entryShape.stableId; shadowedBy now carries the same triple. This represents same-version project/global admissions and multi-version admissions without key collision.
Reserved-list and in-manifest collisions are explicitly unconditional. The DIFFERENT-(stableId, provenance) carve-out is confined to cross-entry live name/alias/root comparisons.

V3-B3/V3-B4's dependency-edge issue is repaired for a truly single dependency-free component: the closure-rule width is restored, versionConstraint-bearing locks are deferred, and TC-ACCEPT names the multi-component member as deferred. V4-B1 concerns the missing cardinality restriction, and V4-B2 concerns the separately unresolved compatibility datum.
